descriptive_statistics.question: When is the median a better summary than the mean, and what does standard deviation measure?
descriptive_statistics.reference_answer: The median is more robust to outliers and skewed distributions. Standard deviation (or variance) measures typical spread of values around the mean.
rubric_points: SD as spread around the mean (1 pt)

data_visualization.question: Which chart would you use for a distribution of a numeric variable versus a relationship between two numeric variables, and why?
data_visualization.reference_answer: A histogram or boxplot shows one numeric distribution. A scatter plot shows association between two numeric variables. Bar charts suit categorical counts.
rubric_points: Histogram/boxplot for one numeric distribution (1 pt)
Scatter for two numeric variables (1 pt)
Bar for categories or equivalent justification (1 pt)

probability_basics.question: State Bayes' theorem in words and why conditional probability is not the same as the reverse condition.
probability_basics.reference_answer: P(A|B) = P(B|A)P(A)/P(B). P(disease|positive test) is not P(positive test|disease) because base rates matter. Conditional probability is probability of A given B, not B given A.
rubric_points: Bayes or equivalent updating formula (1 pt)

distributions.question: When would you use a normal versus a binomial model, and what does the central limit theorem say?
distributions.reference_answer: Binomial models the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials. The normal is a continuous bell-shaped model, often for measurements. The CLT says the sampling distribution of the mean approaches normal for large n, even if the population is not normal.
rubric_points: Binomial as count of successes (1 pt)
Normal as continuous / measurement model (1 pt)
CLT for means / large samples (1 pt)

hypothesis_testing.question: What is a p-value, and what is the difference between Type I and Type II error?
hypothesis_testing.reference_answer: A p-value is the probability, under the null, of data as extreme as observed. Type I is rejecting a true null (false positive); Type II is failing to reject a false null (false negative).

correlation_regression.question: Why does correlation not imply causation, and what does a regression slope estimate?
correlation_regression.reference_answer: Association can be confounded, reverse-causal, or coincidental. A simple linear regression slope is the expected change in Y for a one-unit change in X. Pearson vs Spearman differ in linearity vs rank association.
rubric_points: Slope as change in Y per unit X (1 pt)
Pearson or Spearman mentioned or equivalent (1 pt)

pandas_basics.question: What is a DataFrame, and how do you typically filter rows and aggregate groups in pandas?
pandas_basics.reference_answer: A DataFrame is a labelled 2D table (rows and columns). Filter with boolean masks or query; aggregate with groupby plus sum/mean/count.

data_cleaning.question: Name two common data-quality problems and one way to handle each.
data_cleaning.reference_answer: Missing values: drop, impute, or flag. Outliers: investigate, winsorise, or transform. Duplicates: drop duplicates. Categorical encoding: one-hot or ordinal as appropriate.
rubric_points: Two distinct problems (missing, outliers, dups, types) (1 pt)

exploratory_data_analysis.question: What should a systematic EDA include before you model a dataset?
exploratory_data_analysis.reference_answer: Summarise univariate distributions, check missingness and outliers, visualise relationships, and document findings. EDA informs cleaning and hypotheses rather than jumping straight to a model.
rubric_points: Document findings / inform next steps (1 pt)

statistical_reporting.question: Besides a p-value, what should you report so a reader can interpret a result, and why?
statistical_reporting.reference_answer: Report effect size and a confidence interval, sample size, and a plain-language interpretation. p-values alone do not show practical importance or precision of the estimate.
